title: Mexican and Spanish neighborhood in the French Quarter
summary: Describes the Quarter streets populated by Mexicans, Puerto Ricans and Spaniards, later replaced by Italians, and his Spanish.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Not around chargers and Ursulines anyhow.

Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's right. Because I'll tell you, at that time, at that time in, say, Ursuline Street, you take Decatur Street, you take Dumaine Street. Well, some part of Royal, from, I would say, from Royal and Dumaine, you could say, all the way to Espinade Street was nothing but Mexicans. Mexicans, Puerto Ricans, and Spanish. Yeah. You see? Yeah. That's the only way. And I'm telling you that they were a tough crowd. Like, well, that was it.
Was that around the time of the Spanish-American War?
Oh, no. That was in some ways around, I would say, about 1908, 1907, something like that.
But they had been there for a while then. They were there when you were younger, too.

Oh, well, yeah. They had been there for years. Because it was well populated. That's all. Well, it's just the same thing as you take the French market. We call it the French market. You ain't got a Frenchman around there that I know of. All these Italians, you know? Yeah. They took over.

Yeah. Yeah, just after the period you're talking about. Well, it's the same thing with the Mexicans, little by little, you know, they're scattered around. You understand? Sure. Now, finally, it's very seldom that you see any around. But at the time I was speaking about it, where you just parade around them three streets, like Oisline, Domain, Chauders and that, and that's all you would see was Mexicans.
Yeah. I think by the time World War I came along, the Italians had started getting in there, quite a few of them. Mm-hmm. Yeah, they did.

Well, I did speak Spanish, but I'm ashamed of it now, because I haven't spoke Spanish for years, and I forgot a whole lot. Of course, if I listen at a conversation or something, I'll understand it. But for me to open up a conversation, I'll get started, because there's things that I would like to say, and I forgot them. I can't. You see?
Your parents were Mexicans or Spanish? No, my parents were Mexicans and Spanish.
